A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTSDS2 research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original listening-test results for 20 TTS systems across four domains, objective-metric correlations, and evaluations across 14 languages.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds experiments comparing unweighted and regression-weighted factor aggregation.

M1.justification: The proposed feature set, four-factor averaging, noise references and multilingual substitutions remain unchanged. V2's expanded feature-selection account documents the existing design. The environment-factor removal shown in its Table 1 concerns original TTSDS versus TTSDS2, not a removal between these PDFs.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CLEAN, NOISY, WILD and KIDS speech and the same 14-language benchmark. The new weighting experiments reuse these domains without adding datasets, populations or tasks.

E2.justification: Section 3.5 adds regression-learned factor weights as a comparator to TTSDS2's unweighted mean. The existing objective-metric comparison and 20 evaluated TTS systems retain their membership.

E3.justification: V2 adds domain-level cross-validation, fitting aggregation weights on three domains and evaluating the fourth. Its pipeline prose also replaces previous-quarter collection with collection after the latest evaluated model's publication, although Algorithm 1 still specifies lastQuarter. This documents an inconsistent protocol revision, not established reruns.

E4.justification: New Section 3.5 tests whether learned aggregation weights generalize better than equal weights and examines coefficient instability across training domains. The existing individual-factor correlations, metric-correlation heatmaps and language-distance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Listening-test confidence intervals and correlation-significance reporting are retained. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval procedures or significance tests. Its new cross-validation evaluates generalization rather than estimating uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 4-5 add weighting results: equal weights outperform learned weights on three held-out domains, while KIDS favors learned weights, 0.853 versus 0.606. Existing benchmark tables remain numerically unchanged. Section 3.4 also introduces a bottom-three ranking-agreement claim contradicted by Table 2.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the Gaussian distance expression from W2 to squared W2 and replaces the one-dimensional sorted-sample expression with an inverse-CDF integral. These refine the mathematical formulation; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion soften continual or quarterly benchmark updating into a pipeline capability for recurring renewal. The central claims about robust human-rating correlations, released listening-test resources and 14-language evaluation remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds regularization and ensembling explanations, an MMD-based efficiency suggestion, and discussion of distributional evaluation's misuse implications and language-selection bias. It removes the explicit reference-copying perfect-score example and Appendix C's qualification that leading systems may be indistinguishable within confidence intervals.

D1.justification: V2 discloses the ground-truth feature-selection threshold, five-second video trimming, filtering topics, entailment thresholds and model checkpoint, and provides pipeline pseudocode and survey screenshots. Conversely, it removes the metric-code link, Replicate model identifiers and ParlerTTS modification link. Checkpoint cutoff, model caveats and compute details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for VoiceFixer, WADA SNR, prosody representations and MMD-related alternatives, including Gretton et al. and Jayasumana et al. The objective-metric taxonomy and positioning relative to original TTSDS remain stable; most bibliography changes are stylistic.

P1.justification: Section 2 substantially recasts the notation and metric exposition; the pipeline and conclusion are rewritten. V2 also reorganizes appendix explanations and adds dedicated weighting, ethics and listening-test explanations. Much experimental prose remains, but the central exposition undergoes substantial revision.

P2.justification: V2 removes the opening overview diagram, expands the feature table into a TTSDS/TTSDS2 comparison, moves aggregate results into the main text, and adds two analysis tables, pseudocode and three survey screenshots. It also rotates the detailed results table, removes pitch-example annotations and changes the document layout.

improvement.justification: The weighting ablation in Tables 4-5, corrected distance formulation and disclosed selection/filtering criteria provide a modest improvement in justification and reproducibility of the unchanged metric. Gains are limited by removed access information and new inconsistencies: the collection window differs between prose and pseudocode, and the bottom-three agreement claim conflicts with Table 2. These issues prevent a stronger improvement assessment.
